input.quote: IBM grants Customer an irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, and distribute, within Customer's Enterprise only, copies of Type II Materials.
input.rationale: Section 7 makes Type II Materials the default deliverable category, with IBM (or third parties) holding all right, title and interest, so our rights depend entirely on the licence back. That licence fails the fallback on material terms: it is not perpetual, is not stated to be royalty-free (only "paid-up"), omits any right to modify or sublicense, and is confined to use "within Customer's Enterprise only" rather than for our business. Separately, § 14.18 licenses our contact information for IBM's own business relationship, promotion and marketing-research purposes and permits onward disclosure to Business Partners and assignees, which is independent exploitation of data we supply rather than processing solely to provide the Services. Operation 1 adds the missing licence attributes and business-purpose scope while leaving IBM's ownership of pre-existing tools intact; operation 2 confines IBM's use of our data to providing the Services. We have not disturbed the Type I Materials position (we own those outright), and note the broad Type I licence back to IBM in p0084 as a residual concern outside this rule's checklist.

proposal.summary: Broaden Customer's Type II Materials licence (perpetual, royalty-free, modify, sublicense, for its business) and limit IBM's use of Customer contact information to providing the Services.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is that we receive a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for our business, so we have added those rights to the Type II Materials licence in place of the internal-use-only limit; IBM keeps ownership of its pre-existing tools. We have also limited IBM's licence in our data to processing it solely to provide the Services rather than for its own marketing and Business Partner purposes.
